- Build in short “voice breaks” during your day, especially after long conversations. Even a few minutes of silence can help.

- **Local Backup:** Periodically restore a file (not just view it) from your local backup to ensure the data isn’t corrupted and the backup process is working.

- **File Comparison:** Compare the contents of your source folder and your backup location(s) to ensure all recent files are included.
- **Automated Tools:** Some backup software offers verification or reporting features—enable these if available.

- **Encryption:** Ensure both local and cloud backups are encrypted, especially for health data.
- **Access Controls:** Double-check who has access to your cloud backups. Remove any unnecessary permissions or shared links.
- **Password Management:** Use strong, unique passwords for backup services and update them periodically.

### **5. Update Backup Software**
- Keep your backup software and any related apps up to date to benefit from the latest security patches and features.

- Briefly note the date, method, and outcome of each backup and verification. This can be as simple as a line in your daily log or a dedicated spreadsheet.
